name: Motor-Assisted Bicycle
description: A bicycle or tricycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of not more than 1,000 watts that can carry it no faster than 20 mph on its own, which doesn't fit one of the three e-bike classes; an e-bike with a 750 to 1,000 W motor, or one that otherwise falls outside the classes but is held to 20 mph, lands here. Defined by 23 V.S.A. §4(45)(B) and regulated by 23 V.S.A. §1136(d).

restrictions.rule: A bicycle or tricycle with fully operable pedals
An electric motor with a power output of not more than 1,000 watts that on its own can reach no more than 20 mph on a paved level surface with a 170-pound rider
Not an electric bicycle, motor-driven cycle, motorcycle or ATV
Governed as a bicycle, with a bicyclist's rights and duties
No motor vehicle registration, inspection or operator's license
Riders under 16 may not ride one on a highway
Municipalities may regulate its operation and use by ordinance
